settings.title: Aurora Settings
settings.tooltipsDescription: Show tooltips on hover throughout the IDE.
settings.trustLinksDescription: Open links from the AI chat in your browser without a confirmation prompt.
settings.verboseDescription: Show all compilation messages. Disable to filter (errors, warnings, success, info).

settings.languageDescription: Changes the interface language and the compiler messages language (-pt / -en).

settings.componentsIntro: What compiles and simulates ships with the installer. The rest you download when you need it, and can remove to reclaim space.
settings.aboutThanksText: SAPHO & AURORA are made possible by the support of:
settings.aboutThirdPartyText: AURORA bundles open-source software, each under its own license:
settings.aiIntro: Aurora Intelligence runs on your own API key (BYOK). Pick the provider you have an account with, paste its key, and Save. Keys are encrypted with your operating system's keychain and are only ever sent to the provider you choose.
settings.auroraBg: Aurora Borealis on the Welcome screen
settings.auroraBgDescription: Animated aurora background behind the Welcome screen. It renders on the GPU in a continuous loop; off by default to save battery and to keep weaker machines responsive.
settings.networkWarningDescription: Shows a corner notice on every connection drop. Compiling and simulating do not need the network.
settings.githubForget: Sign out of GitHub and clean now
settings.githubForgetDescription: Removes the access AURORA saved for both accounts and also what the Windows git kept, without waiting for you to close it.
settings.githubForgetOnExit: Clear GitHub and GitLab access when AURORA closes
settings.githubForgetOnExitDescription: On a shared computer, leave this on: closing signs both accounts out of here and of the Windows git, without anyone having to remember.
settings.componentsRemoveBody:
The files of {nome} leave the disk, and whatever depends on it stops working. Getting {nome} back means downloading it again ({mb}), and on a slow network that takes a while.

Your projects are not touched.
settings.componentsBusy: A download is already in progress.
settings.componentsCompileMissing: This machine cannot compile yet: {nome} has not been downloaded ({mb}). Without it, the compile and simulate buttons will not work. Everything is in Settings, Components.
settings.bugReportRowDescription: Describe what happened and send it straight to NIPS-CERN. The screen shows everything that goes along before you send.
settings.componentsDoctorBody:
AURORA will clear the build caches, check the files of every component and re-download whatever is incomplete or broken. Healthy components are not touched, and optional components you never downloaded stay out.

If something is broken, the repair may be a large download.
settings.componentsDoctorHealthy: All good: caches cleared and every component intact.
settings.componentsDoctorFailed: The check could not repair: {lista}. Check the internet and try again.
settings.componentsDoctorNoScripts: The installers folder (components/Scripts) is not on this machine, and without it the doctor cannot repair anything. Reinstall SAPHO from the website installer.
settings.manualIntro: The SAPHO manual ships with AURORA and opens without internet. It updates itself when corrections are published, without waiting for a new version of the program.
settings.manualUpToDate: The manual is already up to date.
settings.manualUpdateFailed: Could not reach the documentation server. The manual on this computer still works.

extended.refresh-button: Refreshes the file tree and reloads project structure.
extended.newProjectBtn: Creates a new AURORA .spf project with the complete folder structure and initial configuration files.
extended.openProjectBtn: Opens an existing .spf project and loads it into the workspace.
extended.projectInfo: Displays detailed information and properties about the currently loaded .spf project.
extended.cmmcomp: Compiles the C± (.cmm) source all the way to Verilog: cmmcomp produces the .asm, then asmcomp produces the processor's .v and testbench.
extended.vericomp: Compiles Verilog (.v) files using Icarus Verilog (iverilog) to generate simulation binaries.
extended.prismcomp: Launches the RTL interactive visualizer to explore processor architectures and signal relationships.
extended.allcomp: Performs a full compilation workflow: C± ➔ ASM ➔ Verilog ➔ Waveform, building the processor completely.
extended.processorHub: Opens the Processor Hub to design and configure new processors, setting ports, memory size, and architectural options.
extended.aiButton: Accesses the AI Assistant to leverage ChatGPT or Claude for help with processor development and troubleshooting inside the IDE.
extended.aurora-settings: Opens AURORA IDE settings to configure preferences and application behavior.
extended.current-spf-name: Displays the name of the currently loaded project.
extended.verilog-block: Browse and insert a prebuilt Verilog module into your project. Most modules are generic and FPGA-agnostic, but always review before integrating.
extended.change-icon-btn: Change the icon of the AURORA IDE. You can select any image file from your computer.
extended.cancel-everything: Cancel all processes and stop the simulation. This will not stop the program, but it will stop all processes and the simulation.
extended.clear-terminal: Clear all content from the current terminal tab.
extended.goup-terminal: Scroll up in the terminal output.
extended.godown-terminal: Scroll down in the terminal output.
extended.export-log: Export the current terminal log to a file.
extended.reload-everything-terminal: Reload the entire application and refresh all components.
extended.filter-error: Toggle visibility of error messages in the terminal output.
extended.filter-warning: Toggle visibility of warning messages in the terminal output.
extended.filter-success: Toggle visibility of success messages in the terminal output.
extended.filter-tip: Toggle visibility of tip messages in the terminal output.
extended.open-folder-button: Open the current project folder in the system file explorer.
extended.close-button: Close the current project and return to the welcome screen.
extended.toggle-file-tree: Collapse or expand all folders in the file tree.
extended.browseBtn: Browse and select the directory where the new project will be created.
extended.generateProjectBtn: Generate the new project with the specified name and location.
extended.cancelProjectBtn: Cancel the new project creation and close the dialog.
extended.projectNameInput: Enter a name, without blank space, for your new project.
extended.projectLocationInput: Specify the directory where the project files will be created.
extended.processorName: Enter a unique name, without blank space, for your processor (used in file generation).
extended.nBits: Total number of bits for the processor architecture (must equal mantissa + exponent + 1 sign bit).
extended.nbMantissa: Number of bits allocated for the mantissa in floating-point operations.
extended.nbExponent: Number of bits allocated for the exponent in floating-point operations.
extended.dataStackSize: Size of the data stack for storing operands and intermediate results.
extended.instructionStackSize: Size of the instruction stack for program execution flow.
extended.inputPorts: Number of input ports for external data communication.
extended.outputPorts: Number of output ports for external data communication.
extended.gain: Amplification factor for signal processing (must be a power of 2).
extended.cancelProcessorHub: Cancel processor creation and return to the main interface.
extended.generateProcessor: Create the processor with the specified configuration.

power.onBattery: On battery ({{level}}%): Windows lowers the CPU clock and simulations run slower. Click for details.
power.dialogOnBattery: This laptop is running on battery. Windows lowers the CPU clock to save energy, so compilations and simulations take noticeably longer, and a long run may be interrupted if the machine sleeps. Plugging in restores full speed; in Windows power settings you can also pick a performance power mode and keep the screen on for long runs. The AURORA already keeps the machine awake while a compilation is running.

bugReport.title: Report a problem
bugReport.whatHappenedHint: E.g.: compiling a .cmm with a matrix, the terminal stops at 40% and nothing happens.
bugReport.expectedHint: E.g.: the build would finish and open the waveform.

1. Open the project
2. Click Compile
3. Wait
bugReport.diagTitle: See the diagnostics that go along
bugReport.consent: By sending, you agree to share with NIPS-CERN the text you wrote above and the diagnostics below. We do not collect the contents of your files, passwords or credentials, nor Aurora Intelligence conversations, and your username is removed from file paths before sending. Even so, some part of the log may still indirectly identify you or the machine. NIPS-CERN handles this data under the LGPD (Brazilian law 13.709/2018): it is used only to investigate the reported problem and is deleted at your request. If you provide an e-mail address, it is used only to contact you about this report.
bugReport.sent: Report sent. Thank you: this is how problems reach us.
